steps.content:
I inspected the data: 45 days (2025-09-01 → 2025-10-15), single account `frHBxlu`, 327 instance families, with `unblended_cost = price × num_instances × 24` exactly.

Findings:
- `qtVJ1PKHrR` (GCP / nOcDI / eTs): price constant at 0.3911 throughout, but `num_instances` jumped from its stable historical band of 7–10 (cost $65.70–$93.86/day) to **35** on 2025-10-13, staying at 35 on 10-14 and 10-15 → cost $328.52/day, a persistent level break and the only resource whose instance count ever exceeded its own historical maximum.
- `23zHd9pKgs` has a big day-over-day move (+$1,600), but that is its perfectly repeating weekly schedule (47 on Mon/Tue, 12 Wed–Fri, 1 Sat/Sun since Sept 1) — recurring baseline, not an anomaly.
- All other resources' deviations are single-digit dollars of jitter (next largest ≈ $12, <5% of the candidate's excess). After reverting only `qtVJ1PKHrR`, the 2025-10-13 total ($10,067) falls right in line with all previous Mondays ($10,065–$10,139), so no residual anomaly remains.

Findings:
- `qtVJ1PKHrR` (GCP / nOcDI / eTs): price constant at 0.3911 throughout, but `num_instances` jumped from its stable historical band of 7–10 (cost $65.70–$93.86/day) to **35** on 2025-10-13, staying at 35 on 10-14 and 10-15 → cost $328.52/day, a persistent level break and the only resource whose instance count ever exceeded its own historical maximum.
- `23zHd9pKgs` has a big day-over-day move (+$1,600), but that is its perfectly repeating weekly schedule (47 on Mon/Tue, 12 Wed–Fri, 1 Sat/Sun since Sept 1) — recurring baseline, not an anomaly.
- All other resources' deviations are single-digit dollars of jitter (next largest ≈ $12, <5% of the candidate's excess). After reverting only `qtVJ1PKHrR`, the 2025-10-13 total ($10,067) falls right in line with all previous Mondays ($10,065–$10,139), so no residual anomaly remains.
